title: Reduce disproportionate commentary
why: A source file has substantially more commentary than comparable files in the same repository, which can obscure the implementation and become stale.
suggestion: Keep comments that explain constraints or intent and remove narration or restatements of the code.
limitations: Requires at least five source files with twenty or more substantive lines.

Generated files, tests, documentation comments, recognized license headers, inline annotations, tooling directives, decorative separators, Shell parameter-removal and path syntax, and files with fewer than ten implementation-comment lines are excluded.

Complete comment paragraphs explaining conditions, rationale (including causal 'so', 'this allows/enables us to', avoidance, and 'without' failure constraints), safety, equations, specifications, examples, or external references are excluded instead of treating their length as evidence of bad code. Blank comment or whitespace-only separators remain part of their block; executable or quoted statements end it. Remaining repository-relative outliers are advisory review prompts, not proof of a defect.

Rust raw and multiline string contents and JavaScript/TypeScript template text do not contribute comment lines. Recognized long reuse licenses and short MIT/SPDX headers are excluded without a fixed header-length cutoff.

Leading shell module comments are excluded when they contain an explicit environment section with named variable descriptions or a Usage/Synopsis section with option or argument notation. Unstructured leading comments, empty contract headings, and comments after the first command remain eligible; this is lexical contract recognition, not shell execution analysis.
